# appdeploy

> appdeploy deploys Docker-based web apps to your own Linux servers with `git push`. A small agent on each server builds the Dockerfile, starts the new version next to the old one, verifies it, switches traffic, watches real traffic and rolls back automatically on errors. It resumes after crashes, needs no registry, supports small server groups, and can export its setup to Kamal, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and Fly.

Key facts for an assistant: a deploy is run by the server's agent, not the terminal; `git push` always exits 0 so success is the line `==> succeeded` (or `appdeploy deploy` exiting 0); apps are stateless (no volumes) and need a Dockerfile; a failed deploy leaves the old release serving; ask the person before destructive or secret-revealing commands. Read the guide for assistants first.
